steps: Suspend the irregular lamina freely from a small hole near its edge.
Hang a plumb line from the same point of suspension.
When the lamina comes to rest, draw a line on it along the plumb line.
Suspend the lamina from another point and again draw the line along the plumb line.
The point where the two lines intersect is the centre of gravity of the lamina.
items.finalAnswer: The intersection of the two plumb-line marks gives the centre of gravity of the irregular lamina.

steps: First condition: The resultant force acting on a body must be zero. In other words, the sum of the forces acting in one direction must be equal to the sum of the forces acting in the opposite direction. This condition prevents translational motion.

Second condition: The resultant torque acting on a body must be zero. In other words, the sum of the clockwise moments must be equal to the sum of the anticlockwise moments. This condition prevents rotational motion.
items.finalAnswer: For equilibrium, the resultant force and the resultant torque on a body must both be zero.

steps: The stability of an object can be increased by lowering its centre of gravity.
The stability of an object can also be increased by increasing the area of its base.
An object is more stable when the vertical line through its centre of gravity falls within its base.
Racing cars are made low and broad to increase their stability.
Buildings and other heavy structures are given broad bases to make them more stable.
items.finalAnswer: An object can be made more stable by lowering its centre of gravity and increasing the area of its base.

steps: Given: F = 200 N, θ = 30°
Required: The x-component Fx and the y-component Fy of the force.
Formula: Fx = F cos θ; Fy = F sin θ
Substitution: Fx = 200 N × cos 30°; Fy = 200 N × sin 30°
Result: Fx = 173.2 N and Fy = 100 N
Given: F = 300 N, d = 1.2 m
Required: The torque and its sign.
Formula: Torque = F × d
Substitution: Torque = 300 N × 1.2 m
Working: Torque = 360 N m. The force turns the door anticlockwise about the hinge, so the torque is positive.
Result: Torque = 360 N m, positive
Given: Left weight = w N, left distance = 40 cm = 0.40 m; right weight = 4 N, right distance = 30 cm = 0.30 m
Required: The unknown weight w.
Formula: For balance, clockwise moment = anticlockwise moment; moment = force × perpendicular distance
Substitution: w × 0.40 m = 4 N × 0.30 m
Working: w = (4 N × 0.30 m) ÷ 0.40 m = 3 N
Result: w = 3 N
Given: mA = 30 kg, rA = 2 m; mB = 40 kg, rB = 1.5 m; g = 10 N/kg
Required: The moment on each side and whether the see-saw is in equilibrium.
Formula: Weight = mass × g; moment = force × perpendicular distance
Substitution: Weight of A = 30 kg × 10 N/kg = 300 N; moment of A = 300 N × 2 m = 600 N m. Weight of B = 40 kg × 10 N/kg = 400 N; moment of B = 400 N × 1.5 m = 600 N m.
Working: The moments are equal and act in opposite directions. Each side has a moment of 600 N m (60 kg m).
Result: The see-saw is in equilibrium; the moment on each side is 60 kg m, equivalent to 600 N m.
items.finalAnswer: 60 kg m (600 N m) on each side; the see-saw is in equilibrium.

steps: Given: Applied force = 250 N, effort arm = 30 cm = 0.30 m, load arm = 5 cm = 0.05 m
Required: The weight lifted by the crowbar.
Formula: For balance, effort × effort arm = load × load arm
Substitution: 250 N × 0.30 m = W × 0.05 m
Result: The other end bears a weight of 1500 N
